snapshot.plan_label: AE 151 (ERA_PLAN): the war ends and the crossing is shut; the next age opens when the northern homeland is fixed by law (SE 1, 22 am Màrt)
snapshot.description: The War of the Hills is over and the crossing is shut. The Administration is gone: its last Commissioner sailed west from Cuan shean with his officers, the Residency above Ros dhomhain stands stripped, the Company's ledgers are ash, and its steamships no longer come. The custodians sit again in their council hall at Cathair dhearg, and the council of the mining country chosen in the forest at Cnoc bheag, with Eilidh nic Raghnaill for its voice, holds the hills, the east, the capital and every coast; its companies, the silver guild's riflemen and the hawk-faithful stand to arms still. Under the truce of Àth àrsaidh the humans left on Dia-thìr, a few thousand of them, go north in columns under safe-conduct into the country of the old concession, where Cathair gheal kept its gates and the Dia-thìrich of the north-west are choosing whether to stay or go south. The pits are flooded or idle, the coal line is broken in three places, the Small-Burning Law is long lapsed, and four children of the coal-blood are alive. The five beacons burn coal again, and their daybooks count no ships.

land_changes.what: Manannan's mist lifted in the winter of the Crossing (AE 1); the western sea is open water at the snapshot, but no ship will come again.
The Rending: the earth torn open along a fault about Cill ghlas (AE 137); the district fenced and closed, left to the thorn.
The Abhainn uaine silted black with the washing of coal (AE 33); its salmon runs failed.
The oak woods about Cathair fhada felled for pit-props (AE 24).
Spoil-heaps at the camps and deep workings of the Muileann chrom district; the lower galleries of the eastern pits at Ros fhionn flooded (AE 150).

new_burgs.name_en: the columns' camp at Baile Mòr ruadh
new_burgs.role: the human families of Ros bheag, Cuan shean, Baile dhìreach and the south-west, received here under the truce
new_burgs.reason: the truce names Baile Mòr ruadh as the place where the columns are received; a few thousand humans in all, most of whom had never lived in the north

new_burgs.role: the Commissioners' house of dressed stone on the rise above the harbour, with its field; stripped of all but its furniture when the council's companies entered
new_burgs.reason: a separate house and grounds above the town from AE 9; entered by the council the morning after Strake left (AE 150); not a later town

new_burgs.name_en: the camp of Cnoc fhiadhaich workings
new_burgs.role: the Company's working opened round Doire mhòr's fields; the gallery that killed eleven; the coughing sickness
new_burgs.reason: the camp at the working is distinct from the hunters' village of Cnoc fhiadhaich (burg 280); it is gone by the present day

polities.name: Comhairle nan Coimheadaichean
polities.name_en: the council of the custodians and the rising
polities.form: the Council of Custodians, sitting again in its hall at Cathair dhearg with its high custodian's seat empty, and the council of the mining country chosen in the forest at Cnoc bheag, which fought the war; custodians, crew-leaders of the Lamp-Watch and dissenting priests of Macha

ruler.name: Eilidh nic Raghnaill
ruler.title: speaker of the forest council
ruler.note: a crew-leader of Baile thais and one of the Lamp-Watch; drafted the second petition. The high custodian's seat has been empty since AE 105.

admin_units.name: Comhairle na Coille
admin_units.name_en: the forest council of the mining country
the custodians of the settlements (nineteen at the first petition, thirty-one at the second)

polities.name_en: the humans' northern country (the concession and the north-west, under the truce of Àth àrsaidh)
polities.form: the human families left on Dia-thìr, withdrawing north under the council's safe-conduct; the concession towns left standing; no Commissioner, no Company; the magistrate of Cathair gheal the only officer left

ruler.title: the magistrate of Cathair gheal
ruler.note: not named; he wrote to both sides asking to be left alone, and the council granted it

polities.name_note: the chronicles give this country no name; it becomes the Tuathaich homeland in SE 1

polities.name_en: the silver guild of Muileann chiar
polities.form: a guild of refiners holding the silver seam and the town under the Silver Compact (AE 44); armed with rifles from the eastern raiders; declared for the council

ruler.note: Ùna nic Choinnich led it at the compact; its head at the snapshot is not named

polities.provinces_note: holds its town and seam within the council's country, no shire of its own

polities.name_en: the Administration of an Tìr Thall and the Company (gone at the snapshot)
polities.form: a Commissioner at the Residency above Ros dhomhain governing by districts drawn for the pits, the customs and the Levy; the Company its partner and at last its master
polities.status: withdrawn: Strake left the Residency (AE 150) and sailed west from Cuan shean with the last ship able to cross; its districts are drawn below as an earlier moment

ruler.name: Lionel Strake
ruler.title: Commissioner (the last)
ruler.note: sailed west; nothing on Dia-thìr tells of his coming anywhere

admin_units.name_en: the districts of the Administration (AE 122 to AE 146)
admin_units.kind: district; the council kept most of their lines as shires in SE 3

the district of Baile Mòr ruadh
units.note: district seat at Baile Mòr ruadh; the kingdom set the seat back at the old harbour

units.name_en: the district of Baile Mòr dhomhain

units.note: the outer coasts, ruled from the harbour office at Seann Vell on Eilean ruadh; its surveyors stopped at the great moss
a customs station on the island, a district of its own
a customs station on the island, a district of its own

diplomacy.note: The humans withdraw into the north-west under the council's safe-conduct; the council leaves the concession towns standing. No column was attacked, and none was helped.
The war ended and the crossing shut on the day of the snapshot.
Cathair gheal sent none of its militia to the Residency; Strake did not answer its letter.

diplomacy.relation: trade in rifles for bar silver

cultures.name_en: the humans of an Tìr Thall (called the Tuathaich from the Severance)
cultures.note: A few thousand left on the island: the concession families of the north-west, and the families of Ros bheag, Cuan shean, Baile dhìreach and the south-west now in the columns going north. Their homeland is called an Tìr Thall; their own name for it was never written down.

orders.name: Òrd Bhrìde
orders.name_en: the custodians' rites of the vein (no ordered body; shrines at the pit-mouths)
orders.note: The Law lapsed when its keeping stopped paying; crews leave the first coal of each new gallery at the shrine of Cill dhìreach; the shrine of Cill ghlas where the word fuil-ghuail was agreed was swallowed by the Rending.

orders.name: Òrd an t-Seabhaig
orders.note: Barred from the camps, its sermons carried in the crews; Ìomhar Seabhag's shrines served the Lamp-Watch and mustered the hawk company for the war.

orders.name: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean
orders.name_en: the druid schools (silent since their last master, AE 123)
orders.note: The hall at Dùn thais shut by Tolley; the masters taught under the trees of Flidais's wood until the last of them died; the register ends.

orders.name: Òrd Mhacha
orders.name_en: the order of Macha, split over the humans' coin
orders.note: The capital's priests blessed the Residency's coin; the dissenters went to the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag and sheltered the forest council; the capital's temple sheltered the locked-out custodians.

orders.name: Òrd na Cloiche
orders.note: Sent no men to the war but shut Inis thais to the Company's ships and gave the hawk-faithful the Fianna's roads.

orders.name: Òrd Mhanannain
orders.note: Held the Crossing the price of a prayer grown slack; its priests at Ceann mhòr taught the first human fishing families the night prayer, and disowned the vigil it became.

faiths.name: Na Seann Spioradan
faiths.note: The first faith to refuse the Company's coal on grounds of belief; the pilgrims of Allt an Àigh through the Long Drought.

faiths.name: An Eaglais
faiths.note: Brought over the sea at the Crossing; the Mission's chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain, a chapel in every camp, its house in the north at Cathair gheal. Its clergy left with Strake; its converts among the overseers' children stay. The vigil of the Grey Night is kept by human labourers near Baile chrom, and called irregular.

bodies.name: Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise
bodies.name_en: the vigil of the Grey Night

routes.rule: A master trail or sea-lane is present when every town it touches stands in this age (or both end towns stand and at most a quarter between are not). The mine road, the queen's road and the crown's old coal-roads are roads; the Company's railway and tram-road are added. The fair road (SE 21) and the lanes dated later are absent.

polities.council: The custodians gave the strangers leave, signed their treaty in a tongue they could not read, and watched their tally ignored, their Law lapse and their hall locked. The council made in the forest at Cnoc bheag fought the war that ended the age, and now sits in Cathair dhearg with the country from the hills to every coast in its hand. It will stand its companies down in the spring and make itself a kingdom.
polities.north: The human families left on the island, a few thousand, march north under the council's safe-conduct into the country of the old concession. Cathair gheal and Muileann àrsaidh kept out of the war; Baile Mòr ruadh receives the columns. They are about to be called the Tuathaich.
polities.silver-guild: The refiners of Muileann chiar kept their seam in their own hands through the whole age, by ledger, by compact and at last by rifle. They sold bar silver to the Company at their own price and paid the raiders in it for guns.
polities.administration: The Commissioners governed from the Residency by districts drawn for the pits, the customs and the Levy, and the Company grew into the office. The last of them locked out the custodians and flew an iron bird over the coal country. He sailed west from Cuan shean and was not heard of again.

burgs.27: Ros dhomhain: the Residency on the rise above it, the Company's quays, the chapel of the Mission; its harbour quarter opened its gates to the council in the last autumn of the war.
burgs.354: Muileann chrom: the Company's pit-town, the overseers' staff that went from father to son to daughter, and the store the war began at.
burgs.44: Baile thais: the town of the first strike, the Lamp-Watch and the book of complaints.
burgs.476: Cathair gheal: the humans' market town of the concession, which kept its gates and asked to be left alone.
burgs.419: Muileann chiar: the silver town, the one place the rising took nothing, because the humans had never held anything there.
burgs.282: Cuan shean: where the humans came ashore in the first winter, and where the last Commissioner took ship.

province_polity_notes.north: The shires that became the Tuathaich homeland (App.H). At the snapshot the concession (105) is human; the rest are Dia-thìreach towns whose people are choosing to stay or go south as the columns arrive.
province_polity_notes.council: Every other shire. The silver guild holds its seam and town inside the council's country; the windy coast (no shire) is held by no one.
